job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT
 
Our client is an established, privately owned Australian business with a diverse portfolio of operations across national and international markets. Operating within a complex, multi-entity environment, the organisation has built a strong market presence and is entering an exciting phase of growth through organic expansion and strategic acquisitions.
 
With a focus on strengthening financial capability, modernising systems and improving commercial visibility, the business offers an opportunity for an experienced finance professional to play a key role in shaping its future.
 
ABOUT THE ROLE
 
Reporting to the CFO, the Financial Controller will take ownership of the day-to-day finance function, leading financial control, treasury, reporting and a geographically distributed team while driving meaningful improvements across systems, processes and financial performance.
 
This is far more than a traditional financial reporting role. You'll be instrumental in building a more efficient, scalable finance function, improving commercial insights and supporting the integration of acquired businesses.
 
With ERP modernisation on the horizon and a strong appetite for automation and AI, this role will suit a commercially minded, hands-on finance leader who enjoys combining technical expertise with business improvement and transformation.
 
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead financial control, month-end and year-end reporting, reconciliations and consolidation across multiple entities.
  • Manage treasury operations, cash-flow forecasting, liquidity and foreign-exchange exposures, including approved hedging activities.
  • Lead, mentor and develop local and offshore finance teams, driving accountability and operational efficiency.
  • Oversee budgeting, forecasting, management reporting and financial analysis to support commercial decision-making.
  • Partner with operational leaders to improve profitability, pricing, project costing, inventory management and margin visibility.
  • Drive improvements across finance processes, internal controls, reporting and data integrity.
  • Play a key role in ERP readiness, systems integration and the adoption of automation and AI-enabled finance tools.
  • Support the financial integration of acquired businesses, aligning reporting, treasury and finance processes.
  • Strengthen audit readiness, financial governance and compliance with relevant accounting standards.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • CA/CPA qualified with substantial experience in financial control, ideally within a multi-entity or internationally operating business.
  • Proven experience in a Financial Controller, Senior Finance Manager or similar senior finance position.
  • Strong technical accounting expertise, with hands-on experience in financial reporting, consolidation and internal controls.
  • Demonstrated treasury capability, including cash management, foreign exchange and cash-flow forecasting.
  • Experience leading and developing finance teams, including offshore or geographically dispersed resources.
  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to partner with operational leaders and translate financial information into actionable insights.
  • Experience improving finance systems, processes and reporting, with exposure to ERP implementation or transformation initiatives
  • Advanced Excel skills and confidence working with complex financial data, automation and modern analytical tools.
  • Exposure to manufacturing, inventory, distribution or cost accounting, including margin and profitability analysis.
  • A proactive, adaptable and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to balance hands-on delivery with strategic improvement.

job.title: Financial Accountant - 3 month contract
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT AND THE ROLE
Our client is an established investment management business seeking an experienced Financial Accountant to join their corporate finance team on an initial three-month contract.
Working within an experienced finance team, you'll provide hands-on accounting support across the business's corporate entities, assisting with day-to-day financial accounting, month-end reporting and maintaining accurate financial records.

This is a practical, hands-on role suited to someone who can hit the ground running, work autonomously and is comfortable getting involved in both financial and transactional accounting tasks. Based in Melbourne CBD, this is a full-time, office-based position with an immediate start preferred. There may be potential for an extension or longer-term opportunity depending on business requirements.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Manage day-to-day financial accounting activities, including general ledger maintenance, journals and accruals
  • Prepare bank and balance sheet reconciliations, investigating and resolving discrepancies
  • Assist with month-end close and preparation of management reporting
  • Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation
  • Support accounts payable, invoicing, payments and other transactional accounting requirements
  • Prepare working papers and assist with BAS and statutory compliance requirements
  • Review accounting transactions to ensure accuracy and integrity of financial information
  • Work closely with senior finance team members to meet reporting deadlines
  • Assist with ad hoc accounting tasks and process improvements as required
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Previous experience in a Financial Accountant or similar hands-on accounting position
  • Strong technical accounting skills across general ledger, reconciliations, journals and month-end reporting
  • Hands-on experience using Xero is essential
  • Good working knowledge of Excel
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline
  • CA or CPA qualified or working towards qualification will be highly regarded
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate financial records
  • Comfortable working autonomously while supporting a broader finance team
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing deadlines
  • Immediate availability or a short notice period will be highly regarded

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT 

Our client is a large and established organisation operating within a complex, high-volume environment seeking an experienced Finance Business Partner to support a key commercial channel.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Commercial Manager, you will work closely with sales, marketing and category stakeholders to provide accurate analysis and practical commercial advice. The role has ownership across customer and product profitability, commercial investment, forecasting, performance reporting and decision support.

This is a hands-on business partnering position for someone who can get underneath the numbers, challenge assumptions and explain where the business can improve performance. You will need to balance commercial thinking with strong financial control and attention to detail.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Partner with sales, marketing and category stakeholders across a key commercial channel.
  • Analyse sales and profitability by customer, channel and product.
  • Provide commercial advice across pricing, promotions, customer investment and product decisions.
  • Manage and analyse commercial spend, including accruals, claims, reconciliations and material movements.
  • Support the financial assessment of new products and other commercial initiatives.
  • Own key elements of the budget and forecasting process across gross margin, marketing investment and operating expenditure.
  • Investigate monthly results and prepare clear commentary on performance, risks and opportunities.
  • Review month-end journals and balance sheet reconciliations across relevant commercial accounts.
  • Deliver accurate daily, weekly and monthly performance reporting.
  • Develop financial models and complete ad hoc analysis to support decision-making.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reporting, processes, controls and commercial outcomes.
  • Take ownership of projects and issues through to resolution.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Degree qualified in accounting, commerce, business or a related discipline.
  • CA or CPA qualification.
  • Strong finance business partnering experience within FMCG, consumer goods or another high-volume environment.
  • Experience supporting major retail customers or a similarly complex commercial channel will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing commercial investment, customer rebates, promotional spend or similar arrangements.
  • Strong understanding of customer, channel, product, price and volume mix.
  • Experience working with large data sets and tracing information across financial systems.
  • Advanced Excel and financial modelling capability.
  • Evidence of using analysis to challenge decisions and improve commercial performance.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the confidence to constructively challenge non-finance leaders.
  • Inquisitive, proactive and comfortable working through detailed issues independently.
  • Able to manage a high volume of work without accuracy slipping.

job.title: Salesforce Support Engineer
job.description:

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Systems Solutions Manager, the Salesforce Support Engineer plays a key role in supporting and enhancing the organisation's core business applications.
 
You'll provide Level 2/3 technical support, administer enterprise systems, manage system configuration and security, and partner with internal stakeholders and technology vendors to deliver reliable, secure and user-focused solutions.
 
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving technical problems, improving business systems, and contributing to ongoing digital transformation initiatives within a collaborative, purpose-driven environment.
 
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Provide Level 2/3 support across enterprise business applications, including incident investigation, troubleshooting and resolution.
  • Experience supporting enterprise business applications in a Technical Analyst, Application Support or Systems Analyst role.
  • Mandatory hands-on experience administering Salesforce (Sales Cloud and/or Service Cloud), including user management, security, profiles, permission sets, configuration, and day-to-day platform administration.
  • Strong SQL skills for data extraction, validation and troubleshooting.
  • Experience supporting user access, security, configuration and data integrity across enterprise applications.
  • Knowledge of system integrations, APIs and data flows.
  • Experience producing business reports and dashboards to meet stakeholder requirements.
  • Understanding of IT service management practices, including incident, problem and change management.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with experience working alongside vendors and cross-functional teams.
  • Excellent analytical, documentation and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Experience within disability services, healthcare, community services or other regulated industries will be highly regarded.
KEY REQUIREMENTS
  • Experience supporting enterprise business applications in a Technical Analyst, Application Support or Systems Analyst role.
  • Hands-on experience administering enterprise platforms such as Salesforce or similar business systems.
  • Strong SQL skills for data extraction, validation and troubleshooting.
  • Experience supporting user access, security, configuration and data integrity across enterprise applications.
  • Knowledge of system integrations, APIs and data flows.
  • Experience producing business reports and dashboards to meet stakeholder requirements.
  • Understanding of IT service management practices, including incident, problem and change management.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with experience working alongside vendors and cross-functional teams.
  • Excellent analytical, documentation and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Experience within disability services, healthcare, community services or other regulated industries will be highly regarded.
WHY JOIN?
  • Join a purpose-driven organisation where technology directly supports frontline service delivery.
  • Contribute to a major enterprise systems uplift and digital transformation program.
  • Work across modern business applications, data, integrations and system improvements.
  • Collaborate with experienced technology professionals and business stakeholders.
  • Enjoy a role that offers variety, continuous learning and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

job.title: Full Stack Developer
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Join a fast-growing travel and lifestyle brand that's redefining the global luggage industry through beautiful, functional design. Founded in 2019, this design-led company has rapidly expanded across Australia, New Zealand, the US, and the UK, with strong international demand and a growing retail presence.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Full Stack Developer, you’ll be a key player in a high-impact internal tech team, working closely with the Head of Technology and stakeholders across the business. You’ll lead the development of digital platforms from ERP and eCommerce to fulfilment and internal tools, focusing on complex, high-value projects that support global scale.
This is a rare chance to grow with a product-focused, fast-paced brand during an exciting phase of international expansion.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Design, develop, and maintain applications across the business
  • Collaborate with the Head of Technology and business stakeholders to scope, build, and deliver technical solutions
  • Take ownership of engineering across internal platforms and customer-facing systems
  • Provide technical problem-solving and contribute to scalable, maintainable system architecture
  • Participate in code reviews and help maintain high development standards
  • Support and collaborate with the offshore engineering team, ensuring alignment on quality and delivery
KEY REQUIREMENTS
  • Strong proficiency in JavaScript, React.js, Node.js, and NestJS, with at least 2 to 3 years of experience building scalable, production-grade applications
  • Experience building and managing CI/CD pipelines using DevOps tools

NICE TO HAVE

  • Familiarity with AI-powered APIs, generative AI tools, or LLM integrations is an advantage
  • Previous experience working in a marketing, digital, or advertising agency environment is highly regarded
  • Understanding of marketing technology, eCommerce platforms, digital campaigns, or customer-facing digital solutions would be an advantage
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, creative, and client-facing environment is a plus
THE BENEFITS
  • Melbourne-based on-site model: office-based with 1 day WFH per fortnight
  • Fast-moving, product-led company culture with a strong design and brand ethos
  • Global growth agenda, this role supports scale across multiple countries
  • Flat structure, collaborative mindset, and high ownership

job.title: Accounts Payable & Payroll Officer
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT AND THE ROLE
Our client is a well-established, growing Australian business seeking an experienced Accounts Payable & Payroll Officer to join their finance team.
Reporting to the Financial Controller and working within a small, supportive finance team, you'll take responsibility for the day-to-day accounts payable function alongside processing payroll for both salaried and operational employees.

This is a hands-on role suited to someone who enjoys transactional finance, has strong attention to detail and takes pride in getting things right. The business is continuing to grow, providing an opportunity to contribute to improvements in processes, systems and reporting.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Manage end-to-end accounts payable processing, including invoice coding, approvals, reconciliations and payments
  • Process weekly and twice-monthly payroll for operational and salaried employees
  • Review timesheets and ensure accurate processing of overtime, allowances and award entitlements
  • Prepare payroll tax returns and assist with superannuation and other payroll compliance requirements
  • Prepare and process recipient-created tax invoices for subcontractors
  • Manage supplier queries and resolve invoice discrepancies
  • Complete daily bank and credit card reconciliations
  • Assist with month-end reconciliations and reporting
  • Use Excel to manipulate, reconcile and prepare data for system uploads
  • Identify opportunities to improve and automate existing finance processes
  • Support the broader finance team with ad hoc accounting and administrative tasks
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Previous experience across both accounts payable and payroll, ideally with 5+ years in transactional finance roles
  • Strong end-to-end accounts payable experience, including high-volume invoice processing
  • Hands-on payroll experience with an understanding of awards, overtime, allowances and statutory obligations
  • Strong Excel skills, particularly manipulating large datasets, reconciliations and preparing data for system imports
  • Experience with MYOB Acumatica, HubSpot or similar systems will be highly regarded but isn't essential
  • Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines
  • Comfortable working within a small finance team and taking responsibility for your own workload
  • A proactive approach to identifying inefficiencies and improving processes
  • Adaptable and comfortable working in a growing business where processes and priorities continue to evolve
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Accounts Payable & Payroll Officer who enjoys hands-on transactional finance and is looking for a stable, long-term position within a supportive team.

job.title: Physiotherapist - Tuggeranong
job.description:
Physiotherapist – Build Your Own Practice | Tuggeranong, ACT
  • Your practice, supported: consulting room, equipment and administration provided.
  • Grow your caseload: connect with onsite GPs and Care Plan nurses.
  • Make the move: relocation assistance available for suitable interstate candidates.
Ready for greater autonomy in your physiotherapy career?
Build your own physiotherapy business within an established multidisciplinary medical centre in Tuggeranong, backed by the infrastructure and support of a large national healthcare group.

This opportunity operates under a Facility Services Agreement (FSA). You’ll receive patient billings directly and pay a facility services fee in return for the facilities and support provided—giving you a way to establish your practice without organising a standalone clinic from scratch.

THE OPPORTUNITY

You’ll deliver physiotherapy care while developing your patient base and building relationships with the centre’s GPs, Care Plan nurses and wider healthcare team.
With bookings, reception and billing administration supported, you can dedicate more of your time to patient care and growing your practice.
The opportunity is available 4–6 days per week, with potential Saturday clinics.

WHAT’S PROVIDED
  • Consulting room, equipment and consumables.
  • Reception and administration support, including bookings, appointment confirmations, patient check-in and billing.
  • Central marketing support to promote your services.
  • Opportunities to develop referral relationships within the medical centre.
  • Relocation assistance for suitable interstate candidates.
ABOUT YOU

You’re a qualified Physiotherapist with current AHPRA registration who enjoys delivering personalised care and building strong patient relationships.
You’ll bring:
  • Sound clinical assessment, treatment and rehabilitation skills.
  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach.
  • An interest in building and managing your own physiotherapy business.
  • The initiative to develop referral relationships and grow your caseload.
WHY TUGGERANONG?

Enjoy life in Canberra’s south, with lakeside walking and cycling, established neighbourhoods and convenient shopping and dining at South.Point.
Tuggeranong combines access to Canberra’s wider amenities with green spaces and an outdoor lifestyle—an appealing base for your next professional chapter.

HOW THE FSA WORKS

You operate your own physiotherapy business within the centre, receive patient billings directly and pay an agreed facility services fee. This is a business opportunity under an FSA rather than a salaried employee position. The fee structure and agreement terms will be discussed with you during the recruitment process.

INTERESTED?

Apply with your updated CV, or contact Vicky at vicky@hassett.com.au for a confidential discussion about the centre, referral opportunities and FSA arrangement.

job.title: Senior Financial Accountant
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT AND THE ROLE
Our client is a privately owned investment group with a diverse portfolio of businesses, assets and investments across multiple sectors. They are seeking an experienced Senior Financial Accountant to join their finance function in a broad, hands-on role.
You'll take ownership of the day-to-day financial accounting, compliance and reporting across multiple entities. This is an opportunity to work closely with senior leadership, gain exposure to a variety of investment structures and business activities, and contribute to the continued development of the finance function.

The role will suit someone with strong technical accounting fundamentals who enjoys being across the detail but is equally comfortable looking for ways to improve processes, reporting and financial controls.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Take ownership of day-to-day financial accounting across multiple entities, ensuring accuracy and integrity of financial records
  • Prepare monthly management accounts, consolidated financial reports and board reporting packs
  • Manage month-end processes, balance sheet reconciliations, journals and general ledger maintenance
  • Prepare BAS, IAS, FBT and other tax compliance requirements, including supporting annual income tax calculations
  • Oversee transactional accounting processes including accounts payable, receivable, bank reconciliations and payroll
  • Assist with budgeting, forecasting and cash flow reporting
  • Manage intercompany transactions, reconciliations and investment-related accounting
  • Support financial reporting and administration across a diverse investment portfolio
  • Liaise with external accountants, advisers and other stakeholders
  • Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes, reporting efficiencies and internal controls
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • CA or CPA qualified with a strong technical accounting background
  • Approximately 4+ years' experience gained within public practice, industry or a combination of both
  • Strong financial accounting, reporting and statutory compliance experience
  • Experience working across multiple entities, including intercompany transactions and consolidations
  • Sound knowledge of Australian taxation requirements including GST, BAS and FBT
  • Strong Xero experience, including general ledger management and reconciliations
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel skills
  • Exposure to investment accounting, trusts or complex entity structures will be highly regarded
  • Experience with investment portfolios, private equity or family office environments would be advantageous but isn't essential
  • Strong attention to detail, organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • A proactive approach with an interest in improving systems, processes and reporting
This is an excellent opportunity for a technically capable accountant looking for greater ownership, variety and direct exposure to senior leadership within a growing investment environment.

job.title: Executive Assistant
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a specialist urban planning and development advisory consultancy that works with developers, landowners and investors to navigate complex planning processes and unlock development opportunities across the Australian property sector. Combining expertise across planning, advisory and project management, they partner closely with clients to deliver commercially grounded solutions while balancing stakeholder, community and regulatory requirements.

Operating as a growing founder-led business, they have built a strong reputation for their collaborative approach, deep industry relationships and ability to accelerate outcomes across residential, retail, industrial and infrastructure-related developments.
 
ABOUT THE ROLE
  
This position is ideal for an experienced Executive Assistant who enjoys operating as a true right-hand support to senior leaders while playing a broader role in the success of the business. Beyond managing priorities, schedules and communication, the role is heavily focused on keeping key initiatives moving, coordinating stakeholder engagement activities, supporting leadership meetings and contributing to the smooth day-to-day operation of a growing consultancy.

It offers the opportunity to become deeply embedded in the business, working closely with the Directors on everything from strategic projects and client events through to operational improvements and business growth initiatives.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Manage complex diaries, inboxes, meetings and executive priorities for the Directors
  • Coordinate stakeholder communication and ensure follow-up on key actions and commitments
  • Prepare board papers, meeting materials and support leadership meetings
  • Assist with business operations, reporting and administrative coordination
  • Plan and deliver client events, networking functions and industry engagements
  • Support marketing initiatives, content creation and the business's external brand presence
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with confidence engaging senior stakeholders
  • Proven stakeholder management capability and the ability to build trusted relationships
  • Highly proactive with strong initiative, problem-solving skills and attention to detail
  • Experience coordinating projects, events and business operations in a fast-paced environment
  • Commercially aware and technically proficient across Microsoft Office and business systems platforms
  • Experience in marketing or business development would be advantageous but is not essential.

job.title: Marketing & Content Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is an established Victorian hospitality group with a portfolio of popular venues across metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria. With a strong focus on customer experience, brand engagement and continued growth, the business offers a dynamic environment where creativity, collaboration and fresh ideas are encouraged.

An exciting opportunity is now available for a talented Marketing & Content Manager to help elevate the group's digital presence, strengthen customer engagement and drive venue-level marketing initiatives.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a varied, hands-on position suited to a creative and commercially minded marketing professional who enjoys taking an idea from concept through to execution.

Working across multiple hospitality venues, you will take ownership of content creation, social media management, digital campaigns and local area marketing strategies. You'll have the opportunity to develop engaging content, build brand awareness and deliver targeted campaigns that attract customers and drive engagement.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Develop and execute engaging marketing campaigns across digital and traditional channels.
  • Create compelling content for social media, websites, email marketing and promotional campaigns.
  • Manage and grow social media platforms, driving audience engagement and brand awareness.
  • Plan and implement local area marketing initiatives tailored to individual hospitality venues.
  • Develop creative marketing materials, digital assets and promotional content.
  • Monitor campaign performance, social media analytics and KPIs to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Support SEO, Google Ads and digital marketing initiatives to increase reach and visibility.
  • Assist with membership and customer engagement programmes.
  • Collaborate with venue managers, internal stakeholders and external partners to ensure consistent brand messaging.
  • Stay ahead of hospitality, consumer and social media trends to develop fresh and relevant marketing ideas.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Minimum two years' experience in marketing, content creation, digital marketing or communications.
  • Previous experience in hospitality marketing, particularly local area marketing, is highly regarded.
  • Strong content creation, copywriting and social media management skills.
  • Creative flair with an eye for design, branding and visual storytelling.
  • Graphic design capabilities and experience producing engaging marketing assets.
  • Working knowledge of SEO, Google Ads and digital advertising.
  • Experience planning, executing and analysing marketing campaigns.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, work autonomously and collaborate with multiple stakeholders.
  • Experience managing membership or customer loyalty programmes.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in marketing, communications, media, public relations or a related discipline.
  • Flexibility to visit venues across metropolitan Melbourne and occasionally regional Victoria.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a highly successful, privately owned business with an established presence across the electrical, air conditioning, renewable energy and infrastructure sectors. With more than 15 years of growth, a workforce of over 40 employees and an impressive portfolio of government, commercial and infrastructure projects, the business has built a strong reputation for quality, innovation and service delivery.

Having established robust operational systems, a loyal workforce and a strong pipeline of opportunities, the business is entering its next phase of growth. An exciting opportunity now exists for an experienced General Manager to take ownership of day-to-day operations, strengthen leadership capability and drive the business forward.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a genuine opportunity to make your mark on an established, high-performing business.

Reporting directly to the Founder and Managing Director, the General Manager will take responsibility for the overall operational, commercial and people performance of the organisation. Leading a multidisciplinary team across operations, projects, service delivery, administration and finance, you will bring structure, accountability and commercial discipline to an already successful business.

A key priority will be transitioning the organisation from a founder-led operating model to a more scalable, independently managed business. You'll work closely with the Founder to strengthen leadership capability, optimise systems and processes, and build the operational foundations to support continued expansion.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead day-to-day business operations across electrical, air conditioning, renewable energy, maintenance and project delivery.
  • Drive operational efficiency, productivity, profitability and overall business performance.
  • Lead, mentor and develop a high-performing management team, establishing clear accountability and performance expectations.
  • Oversee operational budgets, project profitability, labour utilisation, forecasting and resource allocation.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve systems and strengthen operational reporting.
  • Develop workforce planning strategies to support business growth, capability development and succession planning.
  • Strengthen collaboration between operational, commercial and administrative functions.
  • Maintain high standards of safety, quality, compliance and risk management.
  • Partner with the Founder on strategic planning, growth opportunities and business improvement initiatives.
  • Build a scalable operating structure that supports long-term growth and reduces reliance on the Founder.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Proven experience in a General Manager, Head of Operations, Operations Manager or comparable senior leadership position.
  • A strong background in construction, infrastructure, engineering, electrical, trade services, industrial or project-based environments.
  • Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary teams and managing complex business operations.
  • Strong financial and commercial capability, including budgeting, forecasting, cost management and profitability improvement.
  • Experience implementing operational improvements, business systems and scalable processes.
  • A track record of leading organisational growth, change or business transformation.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication and people leadership skills.
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach with the confidence to make decisions and drive accountability.
  • Experience within a privately owned or founder-led business will be particularly valuable, as will exposure to ISO-accredited environments and structured business operating systems.

job.title: People & Culture Business Partner
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a well-established organisation operating within the hospitality and leisure sector, known for delivering exceptional customer experiences and creating a welcoming, community-focused environment.

With a diverse workforce and a strong commitment to its people, the business is looking for an experienced People & Culture Business Partner to support its leaders, strengthen HR practices and help create a workplace where employees feel valued, supported and empowered to succeed.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a fantastic opportunity for a hands-on People & Culture professional who enjoys variety, building relationships and making a genuine impact across a business. Working closely with the General Manager and leadership team, you'll be the go-to person for all things people-related, providing practical HR advice while driving initiatives across employee engagement, recruitment, performance management, workplace relations and organisational culture.

You'll have the opportunity to influence how the business attracts, develops and retains its people, balancing day-to-day HR responsibilities with longer-term People & Culture projects.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Partner with managers and senior leaders to provide practical HR advice and support across the business.
  • Manage the employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, performance management and offboarding.
  • Provide guidance on employee relations, workplace issues, performance concerns and conflict resolution.
  • Develop, implement and maintain HR policies, procedures and employment documentation.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant employment legislation, Modern Awards and workplace regulations.
  • Drive employee engagement, recognition and workplace culture initiatives.
  • Identify learning and development opportunities and support managers with employee training and career development.
  • Oversee workplace health and safety, workers compensation and return-to-work processes.
  • Support remuneration reviews, employee benefits and workforce planning.
  • Use HR reporting, workforce data and employee feedback to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Previous experience in a People & Culture Business Partner, HR Advisor or similar generalist HR role.
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment legislation, the Fair Work Act and Modern Awards.
  • Experience managing employee relations matters and supporting leaders through performance management processes.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to engage with employees and senior stakeholders.
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach and the ability to balance competing priorities.
  • Experience across recruitment, onboarding, employee engagement and learning and development.
  • An understanding of WHS, workers compensation and return-to-work processes.
  • Relevant qualifications in Human Resources or a related discipline
  • Experience within hospitality, leisure, clubs or another operational, customer-facing environment will be highly regarded.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is an established product based business operating across Australia and international markets. With a combination of manufacturing, supply chain and commercial operations, the organisation operates within a dynamic and increasingly complex environment.

The business is entering an important period of growth and transformation, with a focus on strengthening financial capability, improving systems and reporting, and creating greater visibility across commercial and operational performance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the CFO, the Financial Controller will take a broad leadership role across financial control, reporting, commercial finance and business improvement.
This is not a traditional business as usual Financial Controller position. The successful candidate will be responsible for strengthening the financial foundations of the organisation while partnering closely with operational and commercial stakeholders to improve business performance.

A key focus will be improving reporting quality, strengthening controls and developing greater visibility across product profitability, inventory, costing and margins. The role will also play an important part in improving finance systems and processes across an internationally operating business.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead month end close, financial reporting and general ledger integrity
  • Strengthen financial controls, reporting processes and governance frameworks
  • Develop greater visibility across product profitability, gross margins and operational performance
  • Partner with operational and commercial stakeholders to support business decision making
  • Support inventory management, product costing and supply chain finance
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting and FP&A activities
  • Drive improvements across finance systems, processes and workflow automation
  • Support statutory reporting, audit and compliance requirements
  • Partner closely with the CFO on finance transformation and broader business improvement initiatives
SKILLS& EXPERIENCE
  • CA or CPA qualified with strong Financial Controller or Senior Finance Manager experience
  • Experience within manufacturing, FMCG, industrial, wholesale, distribution or another product based environment
  • Strong understanding of inventory, product costing and supply chain finance
  • Demonstrated FP&A and commercial finance capability
  • Strong financial reporting, controls and technical accounting experience
  • Experience improving or optimising ERP systems and finance processes
  • Comfortable working across international operations and with offshore stakeholders
  • Hands on leadership style with the willingness to get into the detail
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively across finance and non finance functions
  • Mandarin language capability will be highly regarded given the organisation's international operations, however is not essential
WHAT'S IN IF FOR YOU?
  • Broad Financial Controller role with genuine commercial and operational exposure

Working alongside GPs, nurses, specialists and allied health professionals, you’ll deliver patient-centred chronic disease management and health assessment services.

Your responsibilities will include:

You’ll bring a proactive approach, strong communication skills and an interest in helping patients manage their health with greater confidence.
